Abstract: The North Saskatchewan River in Edmonton provides excellent exposure of the basal Horseshoe Canyon Formation: characterised by coal-rich paralic successions, these deposits mark the maximum inland extension of the Bearpaw Seaway prior to its eastward regression during the late Campanian. This interval is crucial for stratigraphic correlations across the Western Interior Basin in Canada but has previously been documented only through subsurface data. In this study, we present new U-Pb radiometric dates for bentonite layers and detailed palynological analyses from five stratigraphically constrained sites within the transition between the Bearpaw and Horseshoe Canyon formations in Edmonton.
